sections.en: 1 Walzagora P G : Nalzagora v : Malzagora L : Waltogora M. yesure v : Iesuri M : iesuri G : iesun P : omitted by L. To be read o Syre ('O Syrian') [Steinschneider]. 2 contingit ('it happens') L M P. 3 sphaerica ('spherical') L. corporea ('corporeal') G L M : corpora ('bodies') P v. imaginari seu demonstrari ('to be imagined or demonstrated') L. 4 Alphraganum v : Albaganum L. conclusiones ('conclusions') G L M : quaestiones ('questions') P v. 6 Arabicarum ('of the Arabic') M. 9 caput ('head') v : capit(ulum) ('chapter') M. et caudae et alia ('and of the tail and others') L. 11 Pelusiensem sed alium astronomum ('Pelusian but another astronomer') L. 12 forsan ('perhaps') omitted by G M P. 13 Thildoniae v : Childonus P : Chilvenuz G : Hilzmumi L : Chilmennicz. I suspect the name of Diocletian lies hidden, to whose era the Alexandrians computed years from the 4th century onwards. Indictiones ('Indictions') conjectured by Kroll. 14 ad medium civitatis ('to the middle of the city') v. 15 gradus ('degrees') M v. et tertiae unius ('and of one third') omitted by L. vero ('indeed') omitted by v. 16 gradus ('degrees') v. 17 Alcoharithim G : Alchecharithmi P : Altochanchi v : Alchoharicini L : Alcoleancom M. Gezdagert L (namely the Persian era of king Yezdagerd) : Gerzdagerd G : Iezdagrit M : Gerdagren P : Gedagir v.

sections.text:
¹ Versionem Planispherii Ptolemaei ex arabica lingua in latinam confecit Her-
manus Dalmata, cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 382 b.
² Notus est Ahmed ben Muhamed ben Ketir al Fargânî, astronomus chalifae
el-Mâmûn (cf. Suter, op. cit., p. 18, nº 39). Saepius edita sunt eius Elementa Astro-
nomiae, quae in versione Iohannis Hispalensis incipiunt verbis Numerus mensium
Arabum. Cur Tiberiades ab Alberto appelletur, vide apud Steinschneiderum, l. c.,
p. 365, § 13.
³ De Tebith cf. supra p. 88, n. 4. Compendium eius De definitionibus idem est
atque liber De expositione nominum Almagesti quem Gerardus Cremonensis latine
vertit. Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 387, § 43 b.
⁴ Hunc librum canones Theonis esse suspicatus est Steinschneider, l. c.,
p. 382 c.
⁵ Muhamed ben Musa al-Khowarezmi, astronomus chalifae Al-Mamûn († circa
835 p. C.), composuit tabulas quas Adelardus de Bath latine vertit; cf. Steinschnei-
der, l. c., p. 375, n. 36; Suter, op. cit., p. 10, nº 19.
sections.en:
¹ The version of Ptolemy's Planisphaerium from the Arabic language into Latin was made by Her-
manus Dalmata, cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 382 b.
² Known is Ahmed ben Muhamed ben Ketir al Fargânî, astronomer of the caliph
al-Mâmûn (cf. Suter, op. cit., p. 18, nº 39). Often edited are his Elementa Astro-
nomiae, which in the version of Iohannes Hispalensis begin with the words Numerus mensium
Arabum. Why he is called of Tiberias by Albert, see in Steinschneider, l. c.,
p. 365, § 13.
³ On Tebith cf. above p. 88, n. 4. His compendium De definitionibus is the same
as the book De expositione nominum Almagesti which Gerard of Cremona translated into Latin.
Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 387, § 43 b.
⁴ This book Steinschneider suspected to be the canons of Theon, l. c.,
p. 382 c.
⁵ Muhamed ben Musa al-Khowarezmi, astronomer of the caliph Al-Mamûn († circa
835 A.D.), composed tables which Adelard of Bath translated into Latin; cf. Steinschnei-
der, l. c., p. 375, n. 36; Suter, op. cit., p. 10, nº 19.

summary.headline: Astronomical Canons and Eras
summary.text: Bibliographic discussion of Arabic-to-Latin astronomical works: Walzagora’s Planisphaerium, Alfraganus’s Almagest-related conclusions, Tebith’s De definitionibus, and the Book of Ptolemy’s Canons. It describes planetary-place calculations, the Egyptian and Persian chronological eras, and Alexandria’s longitude and latitude.
